title: The Lymphatic System: Drainage, Surveillance, and Return

info.text: Tissue fluid constantly leaks from blood, and intestinal lacteals absorb dietary fats. The lymphatic system collects both as lymph, screens them in lymphoid organs, and returns them to venous blood.

clusters.name: Lymphoid organs
clusters.fact: Lymphoid organs and tissues house lymphocytes and filter lymph, so immune responses start where lymph is screened.

lymph nodes.text: Small encapsulated filters along lymphatic vessels where macrophages and lymphocytes screen passing lymph for antigen.

spleen.text: Lymphoid organ that screens blood rather than lymph, mounting responses to blood-borne antigen.

thymus.text: Primary lymphoid organ where T cells mature; largest and most active in childhood.

tonsils.text: Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue guarding the throat, screening inhaled and swallowed material.

Peyer's patches.text: Lymphoid follicles in the small-intestine wall that sample antigen from the gut lumen.

bone marrow.text: Primary lymphoid organ where lymphocytes are generated and B cells mature.

clusters.name: Lymph return route
clusters.fact: Lymphatic capillaries collect leaked fluid and intestinal chyle into vessels and two ducts that empty into the subclavian veins.

thoracic duct.text: The body's largest lymphatic vessel, draining most of the body into the left subclavian vein.

lymphatic vessels.text: Valved vessels with muscular walls that propel collected lymph toward the lymphatic ducts.

right lymphatic duct.text: Short duct draining lymph from the upper-right quadrant of the body into the right subclavian vein.

lymphatic capillaries.text: Blind-ended, highly permeable vessels that admit interstitial fluid, solutes, and immune cells.

clusters.name: Fluid and lipid cargo
clusters.fact: Tissue fluid constantly leaks from blood and intestinal lacteals absorb fats as chylomicrons; without lymphatic return that fluid stays trapped as edema.

lymph.text: The fluid inside lymphatic vessels: recovered interstitial fluid plus immune cells and, after meals, absorbed fats.

interstitial fluid.text: Fluid bathing tissue cells, formed from blood plasma leaking across capillary walls.

edema.text: Swelling from interstitial fluid that lymphatic return failed to recover.

lacteals.text: Lymphatic capillaries in intestinal villi that absorb dietary fats into lymph.

chylomicrons.text: Lipoprotein particles that carry absorbed dietary fat through lymph toward the blood.

clusters.name: Surveillance cells
clusters.fact: Lymphocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells patrol lymph and present what they find, turning drainage into immune surveillance.

lymphocytes.text: Immune cells that recognize specific antigen and mount responses inside lymphoid organs.

macrophages.text: Phagocytes stationed in tissues and nodes that engulf debris and present antigen.

dendritic cells.text: Migratory antigen-presenting cells that carry cargo from tissues to lymph nodes.

bridges.fact: Both lymphatic ducts return collected lymph — watery interstitial fluid and fatty chyle from lacteals — to blood at the subclavian veins; that return is what prevents edema.

info.text: The venous endpoint where the lymphatic return route delivers its fluid and lipid cargo back to blood.

bridges.fact: Dendritic cells and macrophages present lymph-borne antigen to lymphocytes inside lymphoid organs such as lymph nodes.

info.text: The handoff where cargo carried into lymphoid tissue becomes a signal lymphocytes can respond to.

lenses.prompt: Which organs screen lymph or blood for antigen?
lenses.explanation: Nodes, spleen, tonsils, and Peyer's patches all screen what flows through them; thymus and bone marrow generate and mature cells rather than screening flow.

reasons.lymph nodes: They filter lymph passing along lymphatic vessels.
reasons.spleen: It screens blood rather than lymph, as the blood-side counterpart.
reasons.tonsils: They screen material entering through the throat.
reasons.Peyer's patches: They sample antigen from the gut lumen.

lenses.prompt: Which concepts carry dietary fat from the gut toward blood?
lenses.explanation: Lacteals absorb fats, chylomicrons ferry them through lymph, and the thoracic duct delivers that fatty lymph to venous blood.

reasons.lacteals: They absorb dietary fats from intestinal villi into lymph.
reasons.chylomicrons: They are the particles ferrying absorbed fat through lymph.
reasons.thoracic duct: It delivers chyle-rich lymph into the subclavian vein.
